title: Using redox-sensitive fluorescent probes to record real-time reactive oxygen species production in cells from mouse carotid body slices
protocol: Prepare cerebellar (CB) slices according to the protocol.
Transduce roGFP probes into CB slices using adenoviral infection.
Measure real-time ROS production in CB slices by microfluorimetry.
Sacrifice mouse with intraperitoneal administration of a lethal dose of sodium thiopental.
Dissect carotid bifurcation under a microscope.
Place the dissected carotid bifurcation in ice-cooled and modified 0 Ca2+ Tyrode’s solution.
Dissect the carotid body from the carotid bifurcation.
Remove the superior cervical ganglion, adjacent arteries, fat, and connective tissues.
Embed the carotid body in 1% (wt/vol) low melting-point agarose in PBS pre-warmed to 42°C.
Quickly place the embedded agarose block on ice for solidification.
Remove the solidified agarose block from the syringe fragment.
Make a smaller agarose cylinder containing the CBs.
Fix the agarose cylinder to a specimen disc with cyanoacrylate.
Place the specimen disc inside the buffer tray of a vibratome.
Fill the tray with cold, modified 0 Ca2+ Tyrode’s solution.
Make 150 μm-thick slices using a standard razor blade.
Transfer slices to a plastic container.
Wash slices twice with cold sterile PBS.
Incubate CB sections with enzymatic digestion solution for 5 min at 37°C in a water bath with shaking.
Transfer CB sections to a 35-mm petri dish.
Wash the sections with cold PBS twice.
Remove PBS completely from CB slices.
Add culture medium pre-equilibrated in a cell culture incubator at 37°C, 21% O₂, and 5% CO₂.
Transduce roGFP probes into CB cells by adding one μl of adenovirus (stock concentration: 1–1.2 × 10^12 viral particles/mL) to 2 mL complete culture medium.
Culture CB sections in a humidified incubator with 5% CO2 and 21% O2 at 37°C for 24 h.
Place CB slices from each mouse (4–6 slices) in a 35-mm petri dish.
Shake the dish slightly and horizontally before placing it in the incubator to avoid slice overlapping.
Replace the medium with adenovirus-free culture medium.
Incubate CB sections for an additional 24 h before microfluorimetric recording of ROS production.
If necessary, cells may be incubated with adenovirus-containing culture medium for 48 h until microfluorimetric recording to allow maximum roGFP expression.
Transfer a CB slice to the recording chamber of microfluorimetric setup, which has been filled with pre-warmed recording solution.
Maintain a continuous flow of recording solution in the chamber.
Pre-warm the recording solution to 37°C and maintain it in a water bath at 37°C during the experiment.
Minimize the volume of recording solution in the chamber to approximately 0.2 ml for faster experimental condition changes.
Maintain a flow rate of the recording solution at about 4 ml/min.
Use a dichroic Di02-R488 filter and a band-pass FF01-520/35 filter for recording.
Select single glomus cells (region of interest, ROI) with strong green fluorescent signals indicating high levels of roGFP expression.
Decrease exposure time right after selecting ROIs to avoid signal bleaching during the experiment.
Establish the acquisition protocol using Live Acquisition software at the beginning of the experiment.
Set spatial resolution to 8 x 8 pixels, excitation time to 20 milliseconds, and acquisition interval to 5 seconds.
Select two fluorescence excitation wavelengths (400 nm and 484 nm) with an emission wavelength of 535 nm.
Record the resulting 400/484 ratio to determine reversible changes in redox state within each selected ROI.
Subtract background fluorescent signal from an area of CB section without green fluorescent signal.
Bubble recording solution with gas mixture containing 20% O2, 5% CO2, and 75% N2 for normoxic condition.
Bubble recording solution with gas mixture containing 5% CO2 and 95% N2 for hypoxic treatment.
Determine basal level redox state of CB glomus cells at the end of the experiment.
Record 400/484 ratio with cyto-roGFP.
Perform in situ calibration of roGFP probes by treating CB slice with 1 mM dithiothreitol to achieve maximum reduction (0% oxidation).
Treat CB slice with 0.1 mM H2O2 to achieve maximum oxidation (100% oxidation).
Pause recording to re-localize ROIs when they move away from the recording region.
Resume recording after re-localizing ROIs.
